Justice Scalia, writing for himself and two other Justices, dissented. Essentially he agreed with Justice O’Connor’s assessment of the
importance of the peremptory challenge system and argued that it did not deny anyone the equal protection of the laws even in the case

NOTES AND QUESTIONS
1. For a discussion of how race affects civil jury access, see Gifford & Jones, Keeping Cases from Black Juries: An Empirical Analysis of How
Race, Income Inequality, and Regional History Affect Tort Law, 73 Wash. & Lee L.Rev. 557 (2016).
2.After Batson, Edmonson, and J.E.B., should it be permissible to exercise peremptory challenges on the basis of religion? See Gendleman, The
Equal Protection Clause, the Free Exercise Clause and Religion-Based Peremptory Challenges, 63 U.Chi.L.Rev. 1639 (1996); Waggoner, Peremptory
Challenges and Religion: the Unanswered Prayer for a Supreme Court Opinion, 36 Loy.U.Chi.L.J. 285 (2004). On the basis of disability? See Benson,
Stricken: The Need for Positive Statutory Law to Prevent Discriminatory Peremptory Strikes of Disabled Jurors, 103 Cornell L.Rev. 437 (2018). On
the basis of gender or sexual status? See Boso, Dignity, Inequality, and Stereotypes, 92 Wash.L.Rev. 1119 (2017).
d.Conducting the Voir Dire
Rules concerning the extent to which the judge or the lawyers conduct voir dire vary among jurisdictions. Federal Rule 47(a) leaves
the matter entirely in the district judge’s discretion. For the range of state practices, see Mize, Hannaford-Agor & Waters, National Center
for State Courts, The State-of-the-States Survey of Jury Improvement Efforts: A Compendium Report 28 (2007).
In SNYDER v. PHELPS, 533 F.Supp.2d 567, 583 (D.Md.2008), reversed on other grounds, 580 F.3d 206 (4th Cir. 2009), affirmed,
562 U.S. 443, 131 S.Ct. 1207, 179 L.Ed.2d 172 (2011), the father of a deceased soldier sued church members who picketed the son’s
funeral “to publicize their message of God’s hatred of America for its tolerance of homosexuality,” and especially its tolerance of
